newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open firmer, outperform U.S. issues.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open firmer, outperform U.S. issues.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened stronger on Monday, with spreads to U.S. long bonds widening, as overnight gains in the Canadian dollar encouraged investors, analysts said.

"It's strictly the Canadian dollar, nothing else major is happening," said Andrew Pyle, head of fixed-income research with ABN-AMRO Bank Canada. "We've seen the breakback from C$1.40 (US$0.7143) and it's got people bulled up again. People are starting to favor Canada over the U.S."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.27 to C$108.90 to yield 7.236 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 1/32 to yield 7.05 percent. The spread between the two bonds narrowed to 19 basis points from 20 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.

The Canadian dollar rebounded slightly in overnight trading, opening at C$1.3969 (US$0.7159) versus Friday's close of C$1.3995 (US$0.7145). Dealers said they were starting to see light at the end of the tunnel for the battered currency, which weakened to two-year lows in recent sessions.
The dollar's recent weakness had prompted speculation the Bank of Canada would be forced to hike short-term interest rates in order to defend the currency.
"You've got very little risk this week in terms of being derailed by surprise events in the U.S. simply because you don't have a lot of information coming out of the States this week," said Pyle.
In other prices, the Canadian 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.21 to C$102.27 to yield 6.674 percent. The U.S. bond rose 1/32 to yield 6.82 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 15 basis points from 13 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.19 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.29 percent.
